title: Participation Volume Is Not Consent Or Legitimacy
summary: A dependency map separating reach and volume from standing, representativeness, evidence, rights, consultation, consent, reasons, legitimacy, and authorization.
map_question: How can participation inform a decision without turning comments, attendance, organizations, or sentiment into automatic consent or legitimacy?
interpretation_boundary: Participation volume may describe salience or reach. It does not establish representative coverage, evidence weight, rights compliance, consent, consensus, legitimacy, decision authority, or a durable mandate.

nodes.label: Standing and constituency coverage
nodes.note: Who participated and who was excluded remain explicit.

nodes.label: Access, safety, evidence, alternatives, voice, and influence
nodes.note: Quality is multidimensional and not collapsed into a score.

nodes.label: Rights, treaty, consultation, accommodation, and consent
nodes.note: Each has its own authority and record.

nodes.label: Reasoned response and residual dissent
nodes.note: Material issues require specific public reasons.

nodes.label: Separate legitimacy audit and mandate decision

links.note: Counts do not reveal missing or overrepresented publics.
Coverage and quality require separate evidence.
Good process does not satisfy every rights or consent duty.
Rights and consultation findings remain in the reasons.

what_this_map_supports: Descriptive reporting of reach and volume with explicit limits.
Separate standing, quality, rights, consent, reason, legitimacy, and authority records.
Retention of dissent and non-consensus after process closure.
what_this_map_does_not_prove: It does not establish that a majority is representative or correct.
It does not infer consent from attendance, silence, continued engagement, or process completion.
It does not generate a legitimacy score, mandate, rank, or policy decision.
next_records_needed: A public record containing submissions, hearings, evidence, alternatives, and dissent.
Separate consent findings where applicable, reasoned responses, legitimacy audit, and mandate receipt.
